issues.legal_issue: A widow’s claim for partition defines her statutory interest in coparcenary property, extinguishes the other coparceners’ right to take that interest by survivorship, and permits the interest to devolve to her husband’s heirs on her death even without division by metes and bounds or exclusive possession.
material_facts: The widow’s husband died while holding an interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property; the finding that he had separated from the coparcenary before his death was not established.
By statute, the widow received the same interest in the coparcenary property that her husband had held.
The widow brought a suit seeking partition and separate possession of that interest.
She died while the suit was pending, before the property had been divided by metes and bounds or placed in her exclusive possession.
Her daughters, as heirs of their father, continued the suit.
issues.conclusion: The partition claim defined the widow’s interest and extinguished the other coparceners’ right to take it by survivorship. On the widow’s death, that interest devolved upon her husband’s heirs, and the decree granting them the share was upheld.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 3(2) and 3(3) of the Hindu Women’s Rights to Property Act, 1937, as extended to agricultural lands in Bihar by Bihar Act 6 of 1942, a widow acquired her deceased coparcener husband’s interest and the same right to claim partition as a male owner. A partition claim defines that interest through adjustment of rights; it does not require physical division or exclusive possession. Once defined by the claim, the interest is no longer subject to survivorship and, when the widow’s estate ends, devolves on her husband’s heirs. The Court relied on Lakshmi Perumallu v. Krishnavenamma and Giria Bai v. Sadashiv Dhundiraj, approved Parappagari Parappa v. Parappagari Nagamma, distinguished Pratapmull Agarwalla v. Dhanabati Bibi, and disapproved the contrary views in Movva Subba Rao v. Movva Krishna Prasadam, Shamrao Bhagwantrao v. Kashibai, and Bhagabai v. Bhaiyalal.

rule.if: widow_partition_proceeding and deceased_coparcener_left_joint_interest and widow_received_substituted_interest and widow_made_partition_demand

predicates.widow_partition_proceeding: The proceeding is a widow’s claim to partition property held by a coparcenary.
predicates.deceased_coparcener_left_joint_interest: The widow’s husband died while holding an interest in the coparcenary property.
predicates.widow_received_substituted_interest: The widow received the same interest in the coparcenary property that her husband held.
predicates.widow_made_partition_demand: The widow demanded partition of her interest, including by bringing a suit for partition.
predicates.defined_widow_interest_devolves_to_husba: The widow’s defined interest passes to her husband’s heirs when her estate ends, rather than passing to the coparceners by survivorship.

issues.definition: When a widow with a substituted interest in coparcenary property demands partition, her interest becomes defined and passes to her husband’s heirs when her estate ends.
